OPPORTUNITY
Description: A university department seeks a teaching assistant for introductory computer science. Responsibilities include leading lab or discussion sections, holding office hours and answering student questions, grading student work and providing feedback, and assisting the instructor with course administration.
Selection criteria: Knowledge of foundational computer science and programming, shown by academic record in relevant courses; written and oral communication skills; interest in teaching beginning programmers; previous teaching, tutoring, or TA experience, including satisfactory past performance; availability for required course duties.

APPLICATION
Applicant TA-v2-456-00199

EDUCATION

MS in Computer Science, Fictional University B | 2025-01 to 2026-12 (enrolled; expected completion)
Undergraduate GPA: 3.51/4.0
Academic and experience record as of 2025-12-31.

RELEVANT COURSEWORK
Introduction to Programming: B | undergraduate, 2018-05
Data Structures: B | undergraduate, 2019-05
Discrete Mathematics: C | undergraduate, 2018-11
Web Programming: B+ | undergraduate, 2020-10
Algorithms: A- | undergraduate, 2019-10

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CSS, Git, HTML, JavaScript, Python

TEACHING AND TUTORING EXPERIENCE
Programming Tutor, University Programming Support Programme | 2025-01 to 2025-05 | 4 months; 6 hours/week

- Prepared practice questions on variables and conditionals for use during individual programming tutoring sessions.
- Discussed debugging approaches during tutoring sessions and asked learners to explain the steps in their solutions.
Teaching Assistant, University Programming Support Programme | 2025-06 to 2025-08 | 2 months; 6 hours/week

- Answered student questions during office hours and prepared worked examples on debugging, lists, and arrays for instructor review.
- Graded programming exercises covering debugging, lists, and arrays using a rubric provided by the instructor.

PROGRAMMING AND COURSE PROJECTS
Study Planner Interface | Web Programming, 2020-10
Scope: individual undergraduate course project.
Project tools: JavaScript, HTML, CSS
- Built a local browser interface with form inputs for a study planner using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
- Documented the study planner interface and the local data flow associated with its form inputs.
Dependency Ordering | Algorithms, 2019-10
Scope: individual undergraduate course project.
Project tools: Python, Git
- Used Python and Git for a dependency ordering project, implementing graph traversal and an ordering routine.
- Tested the dependency ordering implementation against connected, disconnected, and cyclic examples in the course project.
Truth-Table Explorer | Discrete Mathematics, 2018-11
Scope: individual undergraduate course project.
Project tools: Python
- Translated discrete mathematical definitions into Python functions for a truth-table explorer implementation.
- Tested the implementation against hand-worked cases and explained connections between formal definitions and program functions.

COMMUNICATION EVIDENCE
Written communication - course instructor feedback on the project report for 'Dependency Ordering': The report explained the approach clearly enough to follow, with occasional requests for clarification.
Oral communication - course instructor feedback on the project presentation for 'Study Planner Interface': The presentation explained the approach and addressed questions, with occasional requests for clarification.

TEACHING PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE

Teaching Assistant, 2025-06 to 2025-08 - feedback from the supervising course instructor: Supervisor feedback recorded clear explanations, responsive student support, and effective completion of assigned teaching tasks.

TEACHING INTEREST
Interested in university teaching; no specific preference for teaching beginning programmers is stated.

Lab or discussion sections: Available.
Office hours: Available.
Grading and feedback: Available.
Course administration: Available.
